ops.title: MCP "server disconnected" root cause: unreleased manifest bump + installer on the MCP critical path
ops.body:
Session b72f7ef4 (2026-07-22, monorepo/niamey) lost every `mcp__plugin_cc-review_cc-review__*` tool and both `cc-review:organize` agents failed with "No such tool available". The MCP server never connected: the handshake blew Claude Code's hard 30s connect timeout (never retried), logged in `~/Library/Caches/claude-cli-nodejs/<workspace>/mcp-logs-plugin-cc-review-cc-review/2026-07-22T22-04-37-338Z.jsonl`.

Chain: (1) `f0f5423` bumped `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` to 0.21.2 with no `v0.21.2` tag/release — a manual bump, which the autobump `guard-plugins: cc-review` guard cannot stop (it only guards autobump's own bumps; the weekly strict run flags it Mondays). (2) The pinned installer's target became permanently unsatisfiable, so every MCP startup ran `brew upgrade` synchronously in `plugin/scripts/mcp-channel.sh` before the handshake. (3) Two sessions launching concurrently with brew's daily auto-update due serialized on brew's locks past 30s; both lost the toolset for their lifetime.

Fixes shipped 2026-07-22: `v0.21.2` released (tag on `81e89e2`), and cc-skills `99f9f0b` made the shared install-binary fragments detach the refresh when a usable binary exists (plus rename-atomic `$LINK` relinks — bare `ln -sf` could ENOENT a concurrent caller's exec). Consumer repos re-render via their Guides workflow.

Rule to keep: bump `plugin.json` only in the release commit that gets tagged (AGENTS.md § Releases) — a manifest ahead of releases silently degrades every user's session startup until the release lands.
